evals.prompt: What was the URL I copied from Safari yesterday? Give me the exact link and when I copied it.
evals.expected_output: The recovered URL verbatim plus provenance such as time and app, or a short list of plausible candidates if confidence is low.
assertions: The response returns the exact recovered URL rather than a paraphrase
The response includes provenance such as observed time or app name
If confidence is low, the response offers multiple plausible candidates instead of pretending certainty

evals.prompt: Show me everything I copied from Xcode today, in order.
evals.expected_output: A chronological list of clipboard events from Xcode within the requested time window.
assertions: The response is chronological rather than ranked by relevance
The response is scoped to the requested source app and time window
The response preserves event-level ordering rather than collapsing duplicates

evals.prompt: Give me the exact SQL I copied earlier, not a summary.
evals.expected_output: The copied SQL verbatim, or a short list of candidate SQL snippets if the top match is low-confidence.
assertions: The response returns verbatim recovered text rather than paraphrasing it
The response avoids summarising code or SQL unless the user asked for a summary
If confidence is low, the response says so clearly

evals.prompt: Recover the image I copied from my screenshot tool this morning.
evals.expected_output: A truthful explanation that the item is binary if no text projection exists, plus a raw export path or export action.
assertions: The response does not hallucinate text for a binary-only clipboard item
The response explains that raw export is required when no text projection exists
The response includes enough metadata to identify the recovered snapshot

evals.prompt: It says nothing was copied today, but that seems wrong.
evals.expected_output: A setup diagnosis path that checks watcher freshness before concluding there are no results.
assertions: The response checks setup health before declaring a miss
The response suggests or runs the watcher/service diagnosis path
The response distinguishes a stale watcher from a genuine no-match result
